ops.body:
Closed 2026-08-30. All three acceptance criteria met, and both disclosed residuals handled.

**Criterion 1 — cc-runtime has a leg and a refs line.** `ci/fleet-refs.txt` gains `cc-runtime main`; `scripts/fleet-build.sh` `default_repos` gains it too (commit `d9c500a`). `./scripts/fleet-build.sh --ref cc-runtime` → `main`.

**Criterion 2 — nested-module consumers are expressible.** The `<repo>:<module-dir>` grammar landed in `af2dbf5` and is now used by both nested consumers: `cc-skills:plugins/codex` and the newly added `cc-squash:go`. Proved with an empty `FLEET_SRC`: the script reports `no checkout of github.com/yasyf/cc-squash/go` and `.../cc-skills/plugins/codex`, i.e. it derives the nested module path rather than the repo root.

**Criterion 3 — the workflow matrix stops being a third unguarded copy.** The 14-entry hardcoded list in `.github/workflows/fleet-build.yml` is deleted. A new `fleet-set` job runs `./scripts/fleet-build.sh --list | jq -Rsc ...` and the build job takes `matrix: repo: ${{ fromJSON(needs.fleet-set.outputs.repos) }}`. There is exactly one parser: `--list` reuses the script's existing awk readers, and jq only re-encodes its output. The pre-existing `check_refs` cross-validation between `ci/fleet-refs.txt` and `default_repos` is unchanged, so the two remaining copies still cannot diverge.

**Residual 1, `replace ( // comment` leaking its block body — FIXED** (`6b64e80`). `fleet_requires` compared the line's LAST field to `(`, so a trailing comment left `directive` unset and every module in the block body printed as a requirement, putting a peer nobody asked for into a leg's cone. Reproduced against a crafted `go.mod` (the block's `leaked-by-the-bug` module appeared in the output), fixed by testing `$2 == "("` — which a trailing comment cannot move — and re-verified that a plain block and a single-line `replace` still behave.

**Residual 2, an all-hex branch name of 7+ chars refused as a commit — DISCLOSED, deliberately not "fixed".** Nothing distinguishes an abbreviated SHA from an all-hex ref without asking the remote, and the pasted SHA is the mistake worth catching: `git clone --branch` cannot take one, so a cone peer named by a commit would fail at clone time with nothing pointing back at the refs file. Weakening the guard to support a branch name no fleet repo has would be a net loss. Now written into the script's own "Not covered, by construction" section, which is where this task's second criterion says such limits belong.

**Not addressed:** `scripts/fleet-build.sh` still has no automated coverage (`ci/mixedera/gate_test.go` remains the template). That is its own piece of work, not part of these criteria.

**Consequence to expect:** both new legs are RED, because cc-runtime and cc-squash pin daemonkit v0.19.1 and import `daemonkit/{daemon,proc,service,trust,wire,worker}` — packages the consolidation deleted. That is the gate working. Their migration is tracked separately.
